docs.purpose: Shows the full profile page for one building permit — or, for a pre-construction committee-of-adjustment application, a lighter equivalent view — covering its details, which trades it matters to, its change history, the builder, the property and neighbourhood it sits on, related permits, and inspection progress.
docs.data_story: It reads 13 tables — `coa_applications`, `permits`, `permit_trades`, `trades`, `permit_history`, `entities`, `entity_projects`, `permit_parcels`, `parcels`, `neighbourhoods`, `permit_inspections`, `parcel_buildings` and `building_footprints` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `web_permit_detail`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: No SPEC LINK header anywhere in the file. No explicit auth/session check in the handler itself — it is public by route-guard classification. Several secondary joins (parcels, neighbourhoods, permit_inspections, parcel_buildings/building_footprints, linked permits, CoA) are each wrapped in try/catch with comments like 'table may not exist yet' or 'non-fatal' — legacy defensive code that silently returns null/[] on failure rather than failing the request. Core permit and permit_history queries use SELECT *. Called via a template literal from src/app/permits/[id]/page.tsx. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: MOST SERIOUS DISCLOSURE IN THIS GROUP. `SELECT pa.*` (route.ts:152) returns EVERY column of `parcels` to an UNAUTHENTICATED caller. From src/lib/db/generated/schema.ts (parcels pgTable) that includes `parcel_cost_menu`, `cost_fb_total`, `cost_coa_total`, `cost_solar_total`, `cost_garden_suite_total`, `cost_laneway_suite_total`, `cost_garage_total`, `cost_gut_total`, `cost_addition_total`, `cost_kitchen_per_sqm`, `cost_bath_per_sqm`, `cost_basement_per_sqm`, `cost_basement_underpin_per_sqm`, `comparable_builds`, `nearby_builds_summary`, the whole `max_build_*`/`opt_*`/`bylaw_*` block, AND the `geometry`/`geom` PostGIS blobs. This is the EXACT payload that /api/parcels/lookup gates behind a session (401), an active-subscription check (403) and a rate limit, and that src/lib/admin/parcel-lookup.ts:32 deliberately excludes geometry from. Here the same data is free to anyone who knows a permit id, with no auth, no subscription check and no rate limit — a direct contradiction of Spec 100 §5 (docs/specs/03-mobile/100_mobile_parcel_cost_tool.md:111: 'the response is the proprietary cost model — a value payload we will not serve to a lapsed or deleted account'). Reported as a finding, not a fact about intent: I found no spec text authorizing it. THIRD: `SELECT e.*` from `entities` (route.ts:138) returns the full builder entity row; per docs/specs/00-architecture/01_database_schema.md:17 `entities` is the enriched-contact table, and src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:377-385 confirms it carries `primary_phone`, `primary_email`, `website`, `google_place_id`, `is_wsib_registered` — so builder CONTACT DETAILS are served anonymously.
